post.caption:
A battery stores a chemical reaction, not electricity. Two materials that would react are kept apart, with an electrolyte between them that lets ions cross but blocks electrons, so the electrons have to take the long way round through your device. That detour is the current. Rechargeables run the reaction backwards, but never perfectly: each cycle leaves small irreversible structural changes, which is capacity fade. Heat, full charges and deep discharges all accelerate it.
